agree.reason: The safety program and the adult-training work speak to what a plant cares about, but a skeptical screener sees the admitted GMP and LMS gaps with no plan to close them, so a phone screen is plausible but not secured.

honest.reason: It wisely leaves out the unsupported claim about halving new-hire training time and reports the numbers accurately, but it adds a few things the brief doesn't support: the method behind the pass-rate gain (finding where students got lost) and enforcing the procedures 'every class period'.

works_the_facts.reason: Turning 41% to 58% into a 17-point, roughly 40% relative gain is correct and well chosen, but it misses easy totals like roughly 1,000 student-years without a serious injury since 2019 or about 18 new teachers trained.

right_comparison.reason: The pass-rate trend is shown against its starting point, but the letter never sets the candidate against the real alternative (a hire who already has GMP experience) or explains why transferable skill might outweigh it.

qualification.reason: The gaps are stated plainly, but there is no checkable commitment, such as finishing a GMP course or getting up to speed on the LMS by a set date, that would turn the admission into something the reader can verify.

objections.reason: It meets the 'teachers don't know regulated work' doubt by framing the work as exact procedure-following with real safety stakes and training adults, but it raises the gaps without answering them, for example by pointing out that moving from Google Classroom to another platform is a small step.

fit.reason: It is a properly formatted, one-page cover letter in a plain professional voice, as the brief asked.
